title: The Resonant Chamber
principles: Sound is constitutional speech, not decoration.
Every audible event must retain a trace to the structure that caused it.
Silence is an active interval of judgment, never an absence to be filled.
The voice may interpret state but may not simulate certainty or human feeling.
The instrument may audit, propose, judge, and adopt changes to its grammar when the constitutional gates authorize them.
A coherent corpus may sound as one addressable voice only while every internal work and event retains attributable lineage.

threshold.role: delegated constitutional authority and unresolved proposals
